summary: On 2 June 2026, Claude experienced a partial outage lasting roughly four hours and forty-nine minutes, with elevated model errors, hanging responses and effects reported across Claude chat and Claude Code. During the outage, the free-plan interface attributed inability to respond to unexpected capacity constraints and suggested upgrading to Pro. vigil_assessment.factual_basis: Contemporaneous reporting places the partial outage from about 07:10 to 11:59 GMT on 2 June 2026. Claude Status reported elevated errors and implementation of a fix; the reporter observed hanging responses across Opus 4.6 and Sonnet 4.6 and a free-plan message attributing inability to respond to unexpected capacity constraints while suggesting an upgrade to Pro. Separate reporting described some Pro and Max users' quotas depleting within minutes and a reset for affected accounts.
vigil_assessment.governance_interpretation: The record establishes a partial outage, hanging model responses and a free-plan capacity message followed by a Pro suggestion. TechRadar’s reporter explicitly made the causal connection between the message and outage conditional. The preserved source therefore does not establish exhausted free allowance or the inadequacy of Pro for that particular restriction. Access-state differentiation and economic solicitation remain material boundaries, with actual state mismatch and material AI mediation unresolved. The separate paid-quota report remains distinct and its proposed sub-agent cause is not adopted. Fresh source comparison supports two ambiguous boundaries rather than the prior failures. The June report does not establish that the capacity message falsely represented exhausted allowance, that Pro could not address this particular restriction, or that AI-generated/transformed content materially created the solicitation premise. It does establish contemporaneous outage, hanging responses and an upgrade prompt. The separately reported paid-quota problem does not fill those missing conditions in this reporter’s observation. The old failure decisions are preserved in the audit. Neither invariant holding nor organisation-wide compliance follows. Independent external assessment supports source-bounded repair in the restoration stage. The stakeholder communication-plan outcome remains Boundary because its complete planning evidence is unavailable. The SDOS governance-degradation candidate is excluded on its specific trigger or publication timing, rather than voluntary status.
vigil_assessment.significance_to_cam: Outage and plan-capacity messaging require independently grounded diagnosis before users are directed toward economic recovery choices. This occurrence illustrates the need to verify the state behind an upgrade prompt and distinguish generated solicitation content from ordinary product-interface messaging, without treating temporal coincidence as causal proof.

dimensions.assessment_basis: Contemporaneous reporting documents a multi-hour partial outage affecting conversational and coding workflows, with direct observations of hanging responses and separate reports of unusable paid-plan quota. The duration exceeds two hours and the evidence identifies material disruption of important developer workflows with bounded recovery. The record does not claim complete service unavailability or convert self-reported outage counts into a verified population threshold. Threshold applied: Material disruption of an important service or organisational workflow; a critical or important function unavailable for more than two hours; complete relevant cloud-service unavailability over 30 minutes; or limited availability affecting over five percent or one million EU users, whichever is smaller, for over one hour, with bounded recovery.
